To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) in the absence of one parent, the probability of establishing a correct kinship in the child-parent pair is equal to 0.5; (b) the use of the autosomal markers does not allow to increase this probability; (c) the use of additional sets of genetic makers, for example sex chromosomes markers, mtDNA and bi-allele makers, allows to increase the probability of establishing the kinship in parent-child pair to 0.75-0.9.
the kinship analysis based on the autosomal STR locii is not always sufficient for the establishment of kinship relations in the parent–child pairs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the efficiency of using additional genetic markers for the determination of the kinship relations in the parentchild pairs.
the analysis of the kinship relations in the parentchild pairs in the absence of one parent based on autosomal STR markers.

the development of an approach that allows the establishment of a reliable kinship in the cases where it is impossible to determine the relationship between individuals based solely on autosomal STR locus analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the autosomal STRs are not sufficient for the establishment of kinship in the absence of one parent.

the kinship analysis of autosomal markers is a very useful tool for the forensic purposes but it has to be used with a certain caution and it has to be combined with additional genetic markers in order to avoid false exclusions.
in the case of the parent-child pairs the autosomal STR locs are not sufficient for the establishment of kinship relations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of the autosomal markers only is inadequate to solve the problem of establishing the kinship in parent-child pairs.
in the absence of one or both parents the autosomal STR analysis is not sufficient to establish the kinship.
the use of additional sets of genetic marker is necessary for the establishment of kinship in the cases when the autosomal STR locus analysis fails.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of autosomal STR markers is not sufficient to establish the kinship in a number of cases, and that additional sets of genetic marker should be applied to solve the problems of kinship analysis.
it is possible to use additional genetic systems for the establishment of parentage.
